entities.summary: A full-day E11 traverse through the Gauja valley, joining Sigulda’s castle landscape to Līgatne via ravines, forest paths, sandstone outcrops and the Nature Trails corridor.
entities.description: This is the official Forest Trail section 5: a 24 km point-to-point walk from Sigulda Railway Station Square to Līgatne Tourism Information Centre. It leaves Sigulda through the castle and Vējupīte landscape, uses wooden stairs and forest paths around Paradise Hill, crosses the Gauja valley’s ravines and sandstone terrain, and finishes through Līgatne Nature Trails and the historic paper-mill settlement. The published identity does not include the roughly 30 km Visit Sigulda variant or the 26.2 km account’s optional detours.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Independent walkers single out the meandering Gauja, sandstone outcrops and sustained river-valley scenery; the official stage turns those elements into a coherent rail-to-town hiking day rather than a collection of short Sigulda viewpoints.

variants.name: Forest Trail section 5 — Sigulda to Līgatne
variants.description: The official 24 km E11/Mežtaka stage from Sigulda Railway Station Square to Līgatne Tourism Information Centre. This identity intentionally excludes the similarly named roughly 30 km Visit Sigulda route and all extensions or detours.
variants.accessNotes: Point-to-point route. The start is rail-served at Sigulda station. From the Līgatne Tourism Information Centre finish, local buses toward Augšlīgatne are less frequent; confirm the correct pickup and a same-day connection to an onward train or bus before setting out.
variants.seasonalLimitations: Primeval-valley slopes and stairs can be slippery in wet weather and in winter; snow, ice and short daylight materially increase the commitment.
variants.waterAvailability: Carry the water and food needed for an 8–10 hour day; do not treat the Gauja as a safe swimming or drinking-water source.
suitabilityConstraints: A long 8–10 hour walking day with repeated ravine descents and climbs.
Not a step-free or mobility-accessible route.
warnings: The Nature Conservation Agency currently warns of broken trees or damaged infrastructure on this stage; obey closures or detours on site and turn back if passage is unsafe.
Stay on the signed route in protected areas and obey current on-site restrictions.
The Gauja has strong currents and swimming can be dangerous.
This descriptive line is non-navigation-grade; check current Baltic Trails and Nature Conservation Agency notices and use a current hiking map.
